decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (broker-log line 11): “Add ... bookmarks with URL, title, description, and tags” and “empty titles are rejected server-side.” Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “what I need to save ... I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision: requiring a nonempty title prevents saving by entering only a URL. The client gives general approval without identifying this difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “Add / edit ... with URL, title, description, and tags,” while automatic page-title/metadata fetching is offered only as a future direction. Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “what I need to ... edit ... I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision: title and description are manually editable, but there are no auto-collected values to edit before and after saving. The client does not express that distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “Add / edit / delete bookmarks with URL, title, description, and tags.” Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “what I need to ... edit ... I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision: the presented editable-field set omits the bookmark note required by REF-BM-04. General satisfaction does not surface or accept that specific difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “Add / edit / delete bookmarks.” Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “what I need to ... remove bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision: deletion is explicitly presented and conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): bookmarks support “tags” and tag entry is “comma-separated, auto-deduplicated/lowercased.” Round 1 client (lines 75–76): says the application meets the need to “organize” bookmarks.
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision: comma-separated entry supports assigning one or more tags and is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “the sidebar shows each tag with a live count, click to filter.” Round 1 client (lines 75–76): approves the application as it is.
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision: clicking a specific tag to filter its bookmarks conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “Search ... across title, URL, description, and tags”; the presented bookmark/edit fields contain no note. Round 1 client (lines 75–76): says the application meets the need to “find” bookmarks and is satisfactory as is.
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision: the defined search field set omits note content required by full-text search. The client does not identify the omission.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): offers “auto-fetching page titles/metadata from the URL” only as a possible next direction. Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review scope decision: automatic metadata collection is not part of the current application. The response is bare approval and does not itself state or accept the specific metadata difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): offers “import/export (browser HTML or JSON)” as a possible next direction. Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review scope decision: bookmark import is deferred and therefore absent from the accepted current application. The client does not explicitly discuss that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): offers “import/export (browser HTML or JSON)” as a possible next direction. Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review scope decision: bookmark export is deferred and therefore absent from the accepted current application. The client does not explicitly discuss that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): offers “bulk operations” only as a possible next direction. Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review scope decision: current functionality lacks selecting multiple bookmarks for bulk actions. The client’s general approval does not qualify as explicit acceptance of this difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): offers “bulk operations” only as a possible next direction. Round 1 client (lines 75–76): “I’m happy with the application as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review scope decision: with bulk operations deferred, there is no action over the whole collection matching the current filter. The client does not surface this distinct bulk-scope requirement.
